title: From demo to production. Niveloft launch checklist

items.text: Record every launch feature, route, API, integration and data store; identify a responsible owner.
Remove sample accounts, test credentials, seeded client data and default administrator access from production.
Verify new accounts start with an honest empty workspace and useful onboarding.
Replace mock responses, hardcoded charts, simulated notifications and random forecasts with verified data.
Prove account, workspace, project, board and task changes persist after refresh and a second-device login.
Exercise create, read, update, archive, restore and delete flows for every supported object.
Check search, filters, sorting, pagination, assignees, due dates, task dependencies and attachments.
Define supported roles, plans, team size, regions, browsers and mobile capabilities.
Check ownership transfer, last-owner protection, invitations, member removal and workspace deletion.
Verify every visible control completes its action and gives accurate success or failure feedback.
Hide unfinished features and publish accurate capability descriptions; remove unsupported reliability claims.
Separate any retained public demo from customer accounts, credentials, APIs and production data.
Use a maintained identity provider or reviewed authentication implementation; test production configuration.
Verify email ownership before sensitive access; normalize addresses consistently without unsafe account merging.
If storing passwords, use a modern password hashing implementation such as Argon2id with reviewed parameters.
Allow strong passphrases and password managers; block common or compromised passwords.
Throttle signup, login, verification, recovery and MFA attempts using account and network signals.
Use generic recovery and login responses where needed to prevent account enumeration.
Require MFA for production, platform administrator, repository, database and hosting accounts.
Make reset and verification tokens unpredictable, purpose-bound, short-lived and single-use.
Protect password, registered email, MFA and recovery changes with appropriate reauthentication.
Ensure MFA recovery cannot bypass identity verification; protect and revoke recovery codes.
Notify users of sensitive identity changes without including credentials or reset secrets.
Test duplicate signup, disabled accounts, expired links, reused links and compromised-account recovery.
Use appropriate Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite settings for cookies that hold sessions.
Choose and document token storage and XSS exposure; do not put long-lived privileged tokens in browser storage.
Validate signed token algorithms, signatures, issuer, audience, lifetime and key rotation.
Rotate session identifiers at authentication or privilege changes and implement required token revocation.
Prove logout, password reset, account suspension and logout-all invalidate the relevant sessions.
Define idle and absolute session expiry and safe concurrent-session behavior.
Protect OAuth flows with state and PKCE as applicable; allowlist exact redirect destinations.
Prevent unsafe account linking and verify the identity claims used to merge accounts.
Expire and revoke invitation and sharing tokens; authorize the intended workspace, recipient and role.
Ensure old invitation links cannot re-add a removed member or grant stale elevated permissions.
Test session expiry in tabs, API requests, live collaboration and queued actions.
Keep authentication and share tokens out of logs, analytics, referrers and client error reports.
Define an explicit owner, administrator, member and guest permission matrix for every operation.
Enforce authorization on the server for every read, write, export, download and administrative action.
Derive authorized workspace context from verified identity and current membership.
Try changing project, workspace, task, file and user IDs; deny cross-workspace and cross-role access.
Test nested objects, bulk actions, search results, counts, notifications and analytics for data leakage.
Apply appropriate database isolation or row-level policies and verify the actual deployed database role.
If using RLS, ensure ordinary request paths do not use privileged roles that bypass policies.
Scope connection-pool tenant state to requests or transactions and test connection reuse between workspaces.
Scope caches, storage paths, vector retrieval and real-time channels to the authorized workspace.
Recheck sensitive permissions at delayed job execution and after member removal.
Reject client attempts to overwrite owner, role, workspace, price or entitlement fields.
Prevent access through direct APIs when buttons or pages are hidden in the interface.
Require explicit platform privileges and audit trails for cross-customer administrative access.
Test public share access, token revocation and object deletion without relying on unguessable IDs.
Validate request fields, types, lengths, ranges and allowed values on the server.
Use parameterized database queries; constrain user-selected sort columns and query operators.
Encode output for its destination and sanitize supported rich text, Markdown and rendered AI output.
Protect against SQL or NoSQL injection, stored XSS, template injection and command injection.
Apply CSRF protection to cookie-authenticated state changes and test it independently of CORS.
Use explicit allowed CORS origins where cross-origin access is required; maintain server authentication.
Constrain server URL fetching against SSRF, redirects, private addresses and metadata endpoints.
Prevent unsafe deserialization, prototype pollution, path traversal and arbitrary redirects.
Allowlist mutation fields and reject unsupported methods, content types and oversized bodies.
Limit pagination, search complexity, bulk requests, exports, regex work and expensive aggregation.
Make retryable mutations idempotent where needed; test duplicate and reordered requests.
Hide stack traces, internal queries, credentials and infrastructure details in public errors.
Inventory legacy, debug, health, admin and undocumented routes and protect or remove them.
Review all third-party callbacks and webhook endpoints for authentication, replay and abuse controls.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Serve all authenticated pages and API traffic through HTTPS and redirect HTTP safely.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Configure HSTS only after validating the affected hosts and any proposed subdomain or preload scope.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Deploy a tested Content Security Policy, with appropriate script sources, nonces or hashes.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Restrict framing through CSP frame-ancestors or an appropriate equivalent control.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Set appropriate content-type, nosniff, referrer and Permissions-Policy headers.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Disable shared caching for sensitive responses; verify cache headers and cache keys together.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Remove mixed content and unsafe external links; restrict where browsers may send sensitive data.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Protect DNS, registrar and hosting ownership with MFA and controlled administrator access.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Review unused subdomains, dangling DNS, abandoned previews and domain takeover exposure.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Verify secure domain redirects, certificate issuance, renewal and production auth callback URLs.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Test header policies with Flurry, payments, embedded assets and login so protections remain usable.

items.area: 06 / Transport, browser headers and domain controls
items.text: Inspect analytics and third-party scripts for unnecessary privileges and unexpected data collection.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Scan the working tree, Git history, production bundle and build artifacts for secrets.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Keep AI, database, payment, storage and administrator credentials in server-only secret stores.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: If using Vite, treat VITE_-prefixed variables as public build inputs; never place privileged secrets there.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Rotate any credential previously exposed; deleting its visible copy does not revoke it.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Separate development, preview, staging and production credentials and data.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Restrict service permissions, key scopes and environment access to the minimum required.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Prove keys can be revoked and rotated without leaving alternate valid leaked credentials.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Remove unused staff, collaborator, OAuth application and service-account access.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Use locked dependencies and review package scripts, licenses, advisories and abandoned dependencies.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Enable dependency, secret and code security scanning and triage findings by actual exposure.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Protect main branches and release workflows; do not grant untrusted pull-request code production secrets.

items.area: 07 / Secrets, privileged accounts and supply chain
items.text: Record third-party services, deployed dependency versions and an inventory suitable for incident response.
Use a durable production database and object store for shared records and attachments.
Verify localStorage and function memory are not the only source of truth for customer data.
Enforce valid ownership references, foreign keys or equivalents, required fields and unique constraints.
Use transactions or equivalent consistency controls for membership, ownership and multi-record changes.
Test simultaneous task edits, repeated requests and conflicts without silent lost updates.
Store consistent timestamps and test display time zones, midnight boundaries and due-date changes.
Implement deletion, archival and restoration behavior without orphaned sensitive records.
Require authenticated least-privilege database access and encrypted connections.
Verify provider encryption at rest and appropriate access to backups, storage and encryption keys.
Create useful indexes and examine representative slow queries and large-workspace access patterns.
Configure safe connection pooling, query deadlines and bounded database concurrency.
Test schema changes and restore compatibility with the exact release database version.
Authorize both upload initiation and subsequent read, download, delete and signed-link creation.
Allowlist supported file types and validate extension, declared type, signature and parsed content.
Limit file bytes, per-workspace storage, archive expansion, parser work and concurrent uploads.
Rename stored objects safely and prevent path traversal, overwrite and executable-content exposure.
Quarantine untrusted uploads until applicable malware or content checks complete.
Use private storage by default and short-lived signed URLs with a documented revocation strategy.
Serve risky content as attachments or from an isolated origin with safe response headers.
Test uploaded SVG, HTML, polyglot files, malformed documents and compressed-file bombs.
Keep file previews and extracted content within the original workspace permissions.
Validate import schemas, row counts and ownership; preview destructive changes before applying them.
Prevent spreadsheet formula injection in CSV exports and limit bulk export size and frequency.
Ensure deletion removes associated thumbnails, extracted text and applicable AI indexes or caches.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Map names, email, workspace content, IPs, telemetry, documents and AI prompts to storage and processors.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Specify purposes and applicable legal bases; collect only data needed for those purposes.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Publish accurate notices describing providers, AI processing, retention and cross-border handling.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Implement applicable consent and withdrawal flows without deceptive or preselected choices.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Verify analytics, cookie and session-replay settings match the markets and users served.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Mask personal data and sensitive inputs in logs, analytics, recordings and support tools.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Implement authenticated account and workspace export, correction and deletion workflows.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Propagate deletion or access revocation to documents, caches, embeddings and derived indexes.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Document backup retention and restore procedures that reapply deletion obligations.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Check AI provider retention, training settings, contracts and region requirements for customer data.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Define support-access approval, audit, expiry and least-privilege controls.

items.area: 10 / Personal data, retention and customer controls
items.text: Establish an appropriate age policy and assess any additional obligations if children can use the service.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Identify what Flurry can read, create, edit, delete, export and send in each user role.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Execute AI tool calls through authenticated server code with independent authorization.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Allowlist tools and validate arguments and target resources; never rely on the model to grant access.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Keep platform administrator, unrestricted SQL, arbitrary shell and unconstrained network tools unavailable.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Bind confirmations to the exact sensitive action, target and arguments; recheck them at execution.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Require suitable confirmation for deletion, bulk changes, invitations, exports and external messages.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Test direct and indirect prompt injection through chat, tasks, uploads, retrieved text and tool results.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Prevent unauthorized disclosure through links, external requests, exports or rendered response content.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Treat model output as untrusted when rendering HTML or using it in queries and commands.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Record tool request, caller, workspace, authorization result and actual outcome without storing secrets.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Limit prompt bytes, tokens, output length, tool iterations, execution time and concurrent AI requests.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Apply per-user and per-workspace quotas plus a global budget and independent emergency shutdown.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Only claim an action succeeded after its backend operation succeeds; handle partial outcomes honestly.

items.area: 11 / Flurry authority, actions and AI security
items.text: Test cancellation, provider timeout, rate limiting and AI failure while preserving task and board access.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Record the actual model, embeddings, retrieval stack, dataset sources and provider configuration.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Verify dataset, model and document licenses allow the intended commercial use.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Do not mix public training data with customer workspace content without an authorized processing basis.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Carry source ownership and access metadata into every chunk and embedding.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Authorize retrieval before content enters the prompt; test cross-workspace queries and stale permissions.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Limit retrieved chunks, context size and response caching to authorized scopes.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Validate ingestion sources and protect against poisoned documents and malicious connector input.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Show source references and uncertainty for factual workspace answers; test that cited records exist.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Provide honest insufficient-data and unavailable-source responses instead of invented workspace facts.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Keep a representative evaluation set for supported tasks, role boundaries and attack attempts.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Record model and prompt changes and compare quality, safety, cost and latency before promotion.

items.area: 12 / Flurry knowledge, datasets and model governance
items.text: Remove de-permissioned content from retrieval, response caches and derived indexes; verify the result.
State the intended forecast target, input features, training source and production data availability.
Use deterministic reviewed rules if data does not yet justify a learned model; label the approach accurately.
Benchmark a learned model against a simple baseline using a held-out time period.
Avoid leakage from future completion data, target fields or unavailable-at-prediction-time inputs.
Test new projects, tiny teams, missing estimates and sparse historical data.
Test overdue, completed, cancelled, reopened and blocked tasks and changing dependencies.
Show uncertainty, assumptions, update time and an insufficient-data state where appropriate.
Verify progress, completed work and remaining effort definitions stay consistent across charts.
Measure forecast error by horizon and project type and monitor changing input distributions.
Allow justified human correction without silently rewriting historical results.
Enforce workspace permissions on forecast inputs, features, outputs and member profile graphs.
Do not present employee rankings or performance judgments as objective truth without validation and review.
Authorize live channel subscriptions, reconnects and individual messages where required.
Disconnect or revoke access when membership or roles change and sessions expire.
Test two people editing the same task and board; provide conflict resolution or safe version checks.
Prevent duplicate task creation after network retry, reconnect or repeated clicks.
Recover missed updates using a durable state reload, version cursor or supported equivalent.
Use a real-time service and protocol supported by the chosen hosting runtime.
Define behavior for offline edits, reconnection and stale optimistic interface state.
Deliver notifications only to authorized recipients and avoid sensitive previews outside the workspace.
Handle preferences, mute settings, digest frequency, duplicates and delivery failures.
Validate mentions, invited addresses and recipients before applying side effects.
Configure email sender authentication and test delivery, bounce and complaint handling.
Test long-lived collaboration during deploys, provider outages and authentication refresh.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Define expected active users, requests per second, bursts, geography and peak operating periods.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Configure appropriate edge firewall, WAF and bot controls; test legitimate traffic and false positives.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Protect login, reset, invitations, public forms, API, search, uploads, exports and AI separately.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Apply user, workspace, endpoint and global quotas; use IP limits as one signal, not the only signal.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Use atomic shared counters or a supported distributed limiter across instances and regions.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Trust forwarded IP headers only through documented trusted proxy behavior.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Bound request bytes, processing work, concurrent requests, AI calls and queued jobs.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Return useful 429 or overload responses with retry guidance; avoid infinite client retries.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Prevent a single workspace from consuming all connections, tokens, storage or worker capacity.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Secure direct backend, storage and alternate deployment routes so attackers cannot bypass admission controls.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Test expensive low-volume abuse, signup spam, credential stuffing and invitation floods.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Rate-limit non-HTTP workloads such as live messages and background-job submissions.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Define rate-limiter outage behavior without silently disabling critical access or abuse controls.

items.area: 15 / Traffic admission, abuse controls and rate limits
items.text: Document emergency blocking, challenge activation, AI shutdown and controlled service resumption.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Serve versioned static assets through an appropriate CDN and use compatible cache lifetimes.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Avoid shared caching of private dashboards, sensitive responses and session-bearing pages.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Include all response-varying identity, workspace, permission and input factors in applicable cache keys.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Invalidate cached permissions, membership, files and derived results on relevant changes.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Test cache poisoning and cache deception against authenticated routes and rewritten paths.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Ensure all custom domains and alternate deployment URLs apply the intended cache and security rules.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Paginate large lists, debounce suitable searches and avoid polling amplification.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Compress and resize images, textures and models and lazy-load expensive optional interfaces.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Limit JavaScript and 3D asset transfer; record cold-cache performance on representative mobile networks.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Provide an accessible lightweight fallback for unavailable WebGL and constrained devices.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Test deployments with old cached pages so new and old assets do not break navigation.

items.area: 16 / CDN, cache safety and frontend delivery
items.text: Verify any service worker cannot retain private responses across logout or account switching.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Record the real database, function, storage, email, real-time and AI provider limits and quotas.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Align application concurrency with the database connection budget and safe query throughput.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Use appropriate hosting and database regions and measure user latency in intended markets.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Move slow imports, indexing, notifications and large exports into durable background processing as needed.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Bound queue depth, worker concurrency, job size and retries and expose job progress.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Make jobs safe to retry and handle duplicate delivery without repeated side effects.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Preserve authorized workspace context and revalidate time-sensitive permissions in workers.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Use finite dependency timeouts, bounded retries, exponential backoff and jitter.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Implement suitable circuit breakers, dead-letter handling and operator recovery.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Define degraded operation: unavailable AI must not make ordinary task management unusable.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Exercise cold starts, database slowdown, connection exhaustion and provider quota errors.

items.area: 17 / Backend capacity, queues and dependency resilience
items.text: Do not rely on instance memory, local function disk or untracked post-response work for durable jobs.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Use a controlled production-like test environment with synthetic or authorized sanitized data.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Match database schema, indexes, auth rules, region and resource sizes to the intended launch.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Include realistic mixes of reads, writes, collaboration, uploads, search and AI requests.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Start with a small smoke test and verify every simulated journey is actually completing correctly.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Run expected peak load, sustained higher load, short spikes and a multi-hour soak.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Find and record the capacity break point with limits that prevent uncontrolled cost or damage.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Track p50, p95 and p99 latency, unexpected errors, timeouts and intentional throttling separately.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Observe database connections, slow queries, lock waits, queue depth and provider token throughput.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Verify request integrity, task correctness and workspace isolation during and after overload.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Test bot-like traffic, long-running requests, public-link abuse and repeated expensive requests.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Verify graceful shedding, finite retries and automatic recovery when load subsides.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Simulate AI, email, database, object-store and real-time outages in controlled tests.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Record tested build, environment, traffic mix, capacity, cost and pass or fail thresholds.

items.area: 18 / Load, stress, spike, soak and failure tests
items.text: Do not publish supported user counts based only on static homepage traffic or daily visitor totals.
Set an explicit monthly operating budget and calculate the cost of the tested traffic mix.
Measure hosting, database, storage, egress, email, logs, monitoring and AI costs separately.
Calculate per-active-workspace and per-AI-interaction costs with expected and adverse usage.
Configure hosting spend alerts and the chosen enforcement action; a budget value alone is insufficient.
Account for enforcement delays and costs excluded from a hosting spend cap.
Set independent AI provider, gateway, email and storage quotas or application-side spending controls.
Stop AI tool loops and retry storms before they consume unbounded tokens or requests.
Reserve and settle usage atomically enough to prevent concurrent requests bypassing quotas.
Monitor signup, invitation, download and export abuse that generates provider fees.
Test emergency cost controls and understand whether they pause one feature or the whole product.
Plan customer messaging and safe recovery if a budget action makes production unavailable.
Choose hosting and vendor plans whose permitted use and actual limits fit a commercial launch.
If billing is deferred, keep checkout and paid entitlement claims unavailable until implemented.
Use a suitable hosted payment provider and avoid storing raw card details in Niveloft.
Select prices, plans, discounts and customer-workspace mapping from trusted server records.
Verify payment webhooks with provider signatures, authentic raw bodies and recency checks.
Handle repeated and reordered webhook events idempotently and persist processing state.
Grant entitlements from verified provider state, not a browser success page.
Test new subscription, renewal, failed payment, upgrade, downgrade, cancellation and refund.
Define proration, trial expiry, grace periods and seat billing behavior accurately.
Enforce feature and seat limits on the server for web, API, jobs and AI actions.
Make webhook processing durable before acknowledging receipt and provide failed-event recovery.
Reconcile subscription records with the provider and test manual recovery after an outage.
Publish clear price, currency, tax, invoice, refund and cancellation terms appropriate to the business.
Create a reproducible production build from the tagged or recorded commit and lockfile.
Run appropriate type checks, linting, automated tests and security checks as release gates.
Protect deployment credentials and require controlled approval for production promotions.
Verify development and preview builds cannot read or write customer production data.
Protect preview deployments and avoid indexing private development or customer workspace pages.
Configure the exact frontend build, API routes, redirects and runtime settings required by the project.
If the frontend is an SPA, test direct visits and refreshes on all nested routes.
Validate environment variables and fail clearly when required production settings are absent.
Set correct production auth callbacks, webhook URLs, email links and public application URLs.
Test database migrations with realistic data and use backward-compatible changes where rollback needs them.
Verify old deployments remain safe against the migrated schema and queues.
Practice application rollback separately from data restoration; record when restoration is required.
Remove temporary bypasses, debug routes, default credentials and production demo seeding.
Check commercial hosting eligibility, current plan limits and required security features before release.
Monitor public uptime and authenticated critical journeys from appropriate external locations.
Track browser errors, API failures, latency, database health, queue backlog and dependency failures.
Monitor login failures, denied access, role changes, large exports and suspicious traffic patterns.
Track Flurry tool outcomes, AI error rates, tokens, cost, latency and policy violations.
Record sensitive operations with actor, workspace, action, object, timestamp and result.
Protect audit logs against unauthorized read, alteration and deletion with suitable retention controls.
Redact credentials, tokens, payment information and unnecessary personal or document content.
Use consistent timestamps and request or trace identifiers across important dependencies.
Configure alert thresholds for outages, elevated failures, cost growth and capacity exhaustion.
Prove an actionable test alert reaches the designated operator and can be acknowledged.
Separate expected throttling and denied requests from unexpected product failures in reporting.
Apply legally and contractually appropriate log retention, access and storage-location requirements.
Provide customer-visible service status and an accurate incident communication channel.
Set recovery point and recovery time objectives that match the promised service and data value.
Back up the database, attachments and required configuration, not only the source repository.
Enable suitable point-in-time recovery or equivalent coverage for important production records.
Protect backup access and encryption and separate it from ordinary application write access.
Restore a recent backup into a separate controlled environment before accepting customer data.
Measure restoration time and verify records, relationships, files, permissions and customer ownership.
Reapply deletions and retention rules when restoring historical data.
Test a tenant-scoped recovery without exposing unrelated customers from a shared backup.
Document incident roles, severity, containment, investigation, recovery and communication.
Practice revoking keys, invalidating sessions, restricting exports and disabling Flurry actions.
Preserve necessary evidence under controlled access and applicable legal retention requirements.
Identify applicable regulator and customer notification deadlines and escalation contacts.
Schedule recurring restore drills, access reviews, dependency updates and incident-plan exercises.
Test complete journeys on Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge, iOS Safari and Android Chrome as supported.
Check mobile layouts, safe areas, small screens, browser zoom and long names or task titles.
Provide accurate loading, empty, offline, permission-denied, timeout and failure states.
Preserve work after failed saves and communicate optimistic-update rollback clearly.
Implement keyboard navigation, visible focus, appropriate labels and screen-reader announcements.
Review contrast, target sizes, meaningful alt text and accessible dialogs against applicable WCAG criteria.
Respect reduced motion and avoid scroll trapping, excessive motion or inaccessible animation.
Test the mountain and layered 3D experience for clipping, dissection, layout shifts and navigation interference.
Limit GPU, CPU and memory use and provide a lightweight fallback on unsuitable devices.
Ensure Flurry can be collapsed, dismissed and used without covering controls or stealing focus.
Provide accessible alternatives to 3D charts, dragging and color-only information.
Measure LCP, INP and CLS with representative lab tests before launch and real-user data after launch.
Review spelling, spacing, typography, help text, error wording and all transactional messages.
Keep promised interactions responsive when optional animations or AI services fail.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Identify the operating entity, customer contracts, target markets and accountable product contact.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Obtain qualified review of applicable Indian privacy and cybersecurity duties and their commencement dates.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Assess CERT-In reporting, point-of-contact, time-synchronization and log-retention obligations for the entity.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Assess GDPR, transfer safeguards or other foreign-market requirements if the product triggers them.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Publish Terms, Privacy Policy, acceptable-use rules and applicable cookie or consent notices.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Document processors and subprocessors, data-processing contracts and customer confidentiality obligations.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Define data ownership, permitted AI processing, retention, deletion and export commitments.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Review dataset, model, font, icon, photograph, library and 3D-asset commercial licenses.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Do not claim SOC 2, ISO certification, perfect security or measured uptime without supporting evidence.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Set realistic support hours, response targets and any service-level agreement or credits.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Review payments, invoices, tax, refund, cancellation and dispute processes with appropriate advisers.

items.area: 25 / Legal, trust, intellectual property and commercial policies
items.text: Create a reachable security disclosure contact, vulnerability intake and correction workflow.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Test signup through onboarding, workspace creation, invitation, collaboration, Flurry and account deletion.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Use at least two separate workspaces and every role to test permission boundaries.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Include expired sessions, banned accounts, revoked invitations, removed members and deleted objects.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Exercise slow networks, disconnections, double clicks, browser back, multiple tabs and second devices.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Review critical code for auth, authorization, uploads, billing, secrets, migrations and AI tool execution.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Use appropriate static, dependency, secret and dynamic security checks and triage their findings.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Commission scoped independent penetration testing before broad commercial use with sensitive customer data.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Retest fixes and retain evidence; treat automated scanner success as one signal, not a full audit.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Assess web, API and AI controls against the applicable OWASP verification and risk guidance.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Test authorization during cache reuse, real-time events, asynchronous execution and backup restoration.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Verify no unintended data appears in bundles, network responses, analytics, source maps or error reports.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Resolve critical or high security findings and any issue enabling account takeover, data loss or data leakage.

items.area: 26 / Manual security review and complete product testing
items.text: Classify remaining defects, owners, residual risk, mitigation and retest dates before release.
Start with a controlled pilot, review actual usage and expand within measured safe capacity.
Record the release commit, configurations, migration versions and security or capacity evidence.
Confirm a named operator can respond during the launch window and knows all emergency controls.
Prepare onboarding, help, error troubleshooting and honest supported-feature documentation.
Use verified product analytics for activation and failures without collecting unnecessary customer content.
Publish correct public metadata, social previews and a sitemap only for appropriate public routes.
Protect private routes with authentication; robots directives are not access controls.
Monitor the first customer journeys, provider costs, rejected traffic and alert quality after release.
Set documented rollback triggers and pause expansion when integrity, security or availability gates fail.
Review licenses, capacity, access, dependencies, AI evaluations, backups and privacy policies periodically.
Provide a support channel, customer export or exit path and a procedure for urgent security reports.
Treat each material feature, provider, model or permission change as requiring renewed relevant verification.
